newsitem.title: UK: Britain gives $1.6 million to Iraqi hospitals.
newsitem.headline: Britain gives $1.6 million to Iraqi hospitals.

text.p: Britain's Overseas Development Administration said on Wednesday it was giving one million pounds ($1.6 million) in aid to an agency that gives food to hospital patients in Iraq.
"The project involves supplying food high in energy and protein to over 25,000 patients in 127 general hospitals over a six-month period," the ODA said in a statement.
"Most of the patients are poorer members of society. It will help bridge the gap until food provided under (U.N.) Security Council Resolution 986 arrives."

Under the resolution, which Iraq accepted on May 20, Baghdad can begin to sell oil for the first time since August 1990 when U.N. trade sanctions were imposed in response to President Saddam Hussein's invasion of Kuwait.
The deal allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months for the purchase of badly-needed food, medicine and other necessities for its people, suffering under the embargoes.
Britain said it had spent more than 92 million pounds ($150 million) on aid for Iraqi civilians since April 1991.
